sources.label: Showplace Square / Northeast Mission Historic Resource Survey, adopted 2011

historical_record.description: Built by the Market Street Railway as a steam powerhouse, heavy timber framed and brick, generating electricity first from coal and later from oil. The oldest surviving non-residential building in the Showplace Square survey area.
During the 1907 streetcar strike, one of the earliest outbreaks of violence in the district took place outside the powerhouse doors, when armed strikebreakers fired on strikers.

building.builder: the Market Street Railway as a steam powerhouse, heavy timber framed and brick, generating electricity first from coal and later from oil

unknowns: The statement's narrative gives 1893 in one passage and 1894 in another.

historic_survey.eligible_district: Showplace Square Heavy Timber and Steel-frame Brick Warehouse and Factory District (proposed)
historic_survey.physical_integrity: 6 of 7 aspects retained, on the survey's scale
historic_survey.note: The survey rates the architecture 5 of 5. The 2009 context statement gives the status code 3CB; the 2011 survey data table gives 3S, 3CB. California Register criteria cited: 1, 3.
historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 5 means locally significant, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
